Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates dense, sharply demarcated airspace consolidation in the right upper lobe (bounded by the horizontal fissure) and the left lower zone, which is the classic radiographic appearance of typical bacterial pneumonia. This finding aligns with the clinical presentation of fever and neutrophilia, whereas viral pneumonias typically present with diffuse interstitial or ground-glass opacities rather than focal lobar consolidation.
